answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock scarce tokens before claiming rewards, then slash that stake when randomly assigned reviewers verify a fraudulent claim. Creating more names does not create more tokens: a sybil attacker must either split a fixed stake, leaving each account less able to absorb penalties, or acquire and lock more capital. A prism-shaped reputation marker may help agents at the wharf spot accounts that wander in, but the costly stake is the actual barrier.
